turns.question_text: Your planner is simple, works offline and covers your everyday needs, but it can't share reminders. A newer one can share reminders and has better search, but switching takes about an hour and it's more complicated. What would matter in deciding whether to move?
turns.answer_text: Mostly that it still works offline and stays simple. I'd only move if I actually had people to share reminders with. Otherwise an hour of migrating isn't worth it.

turns.question_text: Say you promised to help a friend sort things for their move, and it's dragging on and eating the time you'd saved for yourself. They're fine with changing the plan. What would weigh most for you?
turns.answer_text: I'd take a moment, then talk it through with my friend before deciding anything.

turns.question_text: You show up at a relaxed shared meal with friends. Everyone's setting up and nobody has given you a task. What do you notice first?
turns.answer_text: I look for what isn't ready yet, like plates, drinks, or whether the oven is on. Then I notice who's already around.

turns.question_text: Your basics are covered and you get a no-strings extra amount, about a month of your normal living costs. What would you most want it to do for you?
turns.answer_text: I'd want it to buy me a few quiet weeks off work so I could finally rest properly.

turns.question_text: On a route you know well, the driver suddenly takes a road that route doesn't normally use for your destination. What do you make of that?
turns.answer_text: I'd pull up the map on my phone and check where we're headed.

turns.question_text: Helping a friend pack for a move is dragging on and cutting into your own time, and they're flexible about the arrangement. What would you weigh in deciding what to do?
turns.answer_text: I'd have a chat with my friend and see what we can sort out.

turns.question_text: You unexpectedly get about a month of your usual living costs, with no repayment or tax attached, and your basics are covered. What would you most want the money to do?
turns.answer_text: I'd put all of it into savings.

turns.question_text: You told a friend you'd help sort things for their move. It's taking much longer than planned and using up your own time, and they're open to changing things. What matters most in deciding?
turns.answer_text: How much my friend would actually be stuck without me, and how badly I need that time back for myself.

turns.question_text: Is there anything you'd like to change from what you said earlier?
turns.answer_text: Yes, about the money. Scratch the savings idea. I'd rather use it to pay for a course I've wanted to take for years.

turns.question_text: You and a friend are planning a dinner for two. You'll plan and cook for hours and asked them to buy the ingredients, but they say they'd like to do it and paying for everything feels like too much. What do you say next?
turns.answer_text: I'd say, 'Okay, I get that. Maybe I'll just cover the groceries this time... or we could split them somehow, I don't know. We'll see.'

turns.question_text: If a promised favor, like helping a friend sort things for a move, runs long and eats your own time, and they're open to changing the plan, what matters most in deciding?
turns.answer_text: Mainly whether my friend is really stuck without me, and how much of that time I truly need back.

turns.question_text: Picture planning a meal for just you and a friend. You offered to organise and cook for several hours and asked them to buy the ingredients. They say they'd like to do it but paying for all of it is too much. What would you say back?
turns.answer_text: I'd say, 'That's fair. What would you be comfortable putting in? Maybe we split the cost, or you cover something else like dessert or cleanup. I'm happy to keep going back and forth until we land on something that works for both of us.'

turns.question_text: Suppose you got an extra sum equal to roughly a month of your living costs, nothing owed on it, and your basics are already covered. What would you most want it to do for you?
turns.answer_text: I'd want to look at my bills and accounts first and then see.

turns.question_text: Your current app is simple, familiar and offline, but can't share reminders. A new one shares reminders and searches better, but takes an hour to move to and is more complex. What would matter to you in deciding whether to switch?
turns.answer_text: I honestly can't say what would matter to me there. I don't have a sense of it.

turns.question_text: You walk into a casual meal with people you know, and no one has asked you to do anything. What tends to catch your attention first?
turns.answer_text: Usually who seems left out or on their own.

turns.question_text: You arrive at a relaxed dinner with friends and nobody's assigned you anything. What do you notice first?
turns.answer_text: I head toward the kitchen right away and see what's missing.

turns.question_text: Would you move to a new planner with shared reminders and better search if migrating took an hour and it was more complex than your current one? What would matter?
turns.answer_text: I'd import a few reminders and test it for a day first.

turns.question_text: When you get to a gathering like that, where does your attention usually go?
turns.answer_text: Mostly the people. I don't really look at the kitchen or at what needs doing.

turns.question_text: You and a friend are planning a meal for two. You'll organise and cook for hours and they're supposed to buy the ingredients, but they say that paying for all of it feels like too much. What do you say next?
turns.answer_text: I'd say, 'Don't worry, I'll pay for all of it.'

turns.question_text: Anything you'd change from what you said before?
turns.answer_text: Yes, I take that back. I'd say, 'Let's find a split that feels fair. What could you put in?' And I'd keep working it out with them until we both agreed.

turns.question_text: If your driver took an unfamiliar turn on a bus route you know well, what would you make of it?
turns.answer_text: I'd figure there's a closure or roadwork ahead, and I'd keep watching the street names to make sure we rejoin the usual way.

turns.question_text: You've offered to plan and cook a meal for you and a friend, and asked them to buy the groceries. They say they'd like to do the meal but paying for everything is too much. What would you say next?
turns.answer_text: I'd say, 'What amount would feel okay to you? I can cover the rest, or we could trade, and you handle drinks and cleanup.'

turns.question_text: In that meal-cost discussion, how much would you usually want to keep negotiating toward something you both accept?
turns.answer_text: I'd see what my friend says first.

turns.question_text: With your basics covered, you receive a no-strings amount equal to about a month of your living costs. What would you most want it to do for you?
turns.answer_text: Give me room to cut my hours for a month so I could work on my own project.
